post.caption:
A transistor is a switch, and that is the whole story. Vacuum tubes did the same job the size of a thumb and burned out constantly; transistors do it in solid material with nothing to wear out. Wire a few together and you get a logic gate, wire gates together and you get arithmetic. The count doubled roughly every two years for decades, and features are now a handful of nanometres, only tens of atoms across, which is exactly why the doubling is slowing.
